The buyer of a put pays a premium and has the right to sell at the strike. Maximum loss is the premium; profit rises as the price falls to zero.
mocks.w: Correct: The buyer of a put pays a premium and has the right to sell at the strike. Maximum loss is the premium; profit rises as the price falls to zero.

mocks.p: Option prices suggest the market expects larger swings. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Implied volatility
Time value
European option
Exercise and assignment
mocks.w: This is Implied volatility. Implied volatility is the volatility the market's option prices imply for the underlying, derived from the option price.

mocks.p: A contract with a fixed lot size, expiry and daily settlement. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Swap
Exchange-traded derivative
Futures contract
Over-the-counter derivative
mocks.w: This is Exchange-traded derivative. Exchange-traded derivatives have standardised terms, are cleared by a clearing corporation and carry lower counterparty risk.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Put-call parity” is correct?
o: For European options, the call price minus the put price equals the present value relationship of spot and strike; deviations offer arbitrage.
A long call's break-even is strike minus premium.
Calls and puts are priced independently.
A call buyer has unlimited loss.
mocks.w: Correct: For European options, the call price minus the put price equals the present value relationship of spot and strike; deviations offer arbitrage.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Index options are cash settled at expiry on the closing index value; in-the-money options are exercised automatically.
o: Long put payoff
Call option buyer
American option
Settlement of index options
mocks.w: Settlement of index options: Index options are cash settled at expiry on the closing index value; in-the-money options are exercised automatically.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Option chain” is correct?
o: A short call is profitable at any rise in price.
An option chain lists the available strikes and premiums of calls and puts for a given underlying and expiry.
An option chain shows only futures prices.
A European option holder may exercise any day.
mocks.w: Correct: An option chain lists the available strikes and premiums of calls and puts for a given underlying and expiry.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Tax audit” is correct?
o: Turnover for F&O is equal to the contract value.
F&O losses can never be carried forward.
Tax audit is never required for traders.
A person whose derivatives turnover or losses cross specified thresholds may need to get accounts audited under the tax law.
mocks.w: Correct: A person whose derivatives turnover or losses cross specified thresholds may need to get accounts audited under the tax law.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Initial margin” is correct?
o: Initial margin is refunded as profit after the first day.
Initial margin is the upfront deposit collected to cover the potential loss on a futures position over a short period. It is risk-based, using the SPAN system.
Exposure margin replaces SPAN margin entirely.
Stock futures are always cash settled.
mocks.w: Correct: Initial margin is the upfront deposit collected to cover the potential loss on a futures position over a short period. It is risk-based, using the SPAN system.

mocks.p: A holder can exercise whenever she chooses before expiry. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: At-the-money
Gamma
American option
Call option seller
mocks.w: This is American option. An American option can be exercised at any time up to and including expiry.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Vega” is correct?
o: Vega measures the effect of interest rate changes.
Time value rises as expiry approaches.
An at-the-money option has high intrinsic value.
Vega measures the change in an option's price for a 1% change in volatility. Higher volatility raises both call and put prices.
mocks.w: Correct: Vega measures the change in an option's price for a 1% change in volatility. Higher volatility raises both call and put prices.

mocks.p: An exchange-traded contract in which both parties must settle at expiry. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Futures contract
Price discovery
Over-the-counter derivative
Swap
mocks.w: This is Futures contract. A futures contract is a standardised agreement traded on an exchange to buy or sell an underlying at a fixed price on a future date, with the clearing corporation guaranteeing performance.

mocks.p: A fund manager sells index futures to offset a possible fall in her holdings. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Hedging with index futures
Contract specification
Long hedge versus short hedge
Initial margin
mocks.w: This is Hedging with index futures. A portfolio owner can sell index futures to protect against a fall in the market; the number of contracts depends on portfolio value and beta.

mocks.p: A trader can square off but cannot build new positions in a stock under restriction. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Market maker
Trading hours of derivatives
Ban period
Client position limit
mocks.w: This is Ban period. In the ban period, traders can only reduce their open positions in the stock; fresh positions are not allowed.

mocks.p: A writer who sold a 500 put at ₹15 loses below 485. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: At-the-money
Call option seller
Rho
Short put payoff
mocks.w: This is Short put payoff. A short put's profit at expiry = premium − max(strike − spot, 0); break-even = strike − premium.

mocks.p: A stock must meet liquidity and size tests to get derivatives contracts. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Eligibility of stocks
Investor Protection Fund
Trading member
Certification requirement
mocks.w: This is Eligibility of stocks. Stocks are admitted to derivatives based on criteria such as market capitalisation, free float, trading frequency and volatility.

mocks.p: A trader ends an option position by selling it before expiry. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Mark-to-market margin
Default handling
Position squaring and exercise
Professional clearing member
mocks.w: This is Position squaring and exercise. A position can be closed by an opposite trade or held to expiry, when options are exercised or lapse and futures are settled.

mocks.p: A trader buys shares and sells the future, locking in a gap. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Single-stock futures
Expiry cycle
Cash-and-carry arbitrage
Long hedge versus short hedge
mocks.w: This is Cash-and-carry arbitrage. Cash-and-carry arbitrage buys the underlying in the cash market and sells the future when the future is expensive relative to fair value.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Proprietary versus client trades” is correct?
o: Proprietary and client trades are mixed together.
Suitability is irrelevant to broking.
Brokers must distinguish their own proprietary trades from client trades and ensure they are reported and handled separately.
Brokers may use client funds for their own trades.
mocks.w: Correct: Brokers must distinguish their own proprietary trades from client trades and ensure they are reported and handled separately.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Mark-to-market margin” is correct?
o: The daily settlement price is the opening price.
MTM margin is collected from members for the day's losses on open positions, to ensure daily settlement.
The fund is paid to investors as dividend.
MTM margin is collected only at expiry.
mocks.w: Correct: MTM margin is collected from members for the day's losses on open positions, to ensure daily settlement.

mocks.p: A trader sells a future at 24,000 and it closes at 23,900. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Short futures position
Basis
Expiry cycle
Backwardation
mocks.w: This is Short futures position. A short position sells the contract and gains when the price falls below the entry price and loses when it rises.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Haircut” is correct?
o: A haircut increases the collateral value.
Extreme loss margin is the same as premium.
A haircut is a reduction applied to the value of collateral securities to protect against price falls.
Positions cannot be closed before expiry.
mocks.w: Correct: A haircut is a reduction applied to the value of collateral securities to protect against price falls.

mocks.p: A small tax is deducted on the sell side of a futures trade. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Mark-to-market accounting
Carry forward of business losses
Securities transaction tax on derivatives
Turnover for derivatives
mocks.w: This is Securities transaction tax on derivatives. STT is charged on derivatives transactions, for example on the sale of options on the premium and on futures sale, at rates set by law.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? The cost of carry is the cost of holding the underlying until expiry, mainly financing cost less any income such as dividends, and drives futures pricing.
o: Cash-and-carry arbitrage
Contract specification
Cost of carry
Expiry cycle
mocks.w: Cost of carry: The cost of carry is the cost of holding the underlying until expiry, mainly financing cost less any income such as dividends, and drives futures pricing.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Covered call” is correct?
o: A covered call has unlimited upside.
A covered call holds the underlying and sells a call against it, earning the premium but capping the upside.
A protective put adds to the loss when prices fall.
A butterfly spread profits from a large move.
mocks.w: Correct: A covered call holds the underlying and sells a call against it, earning the premium but capping the upside.

mocks.p: A seller deposits margin while the buyer only pays the premium. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Option writer margin
Long put payoff
Rho
Vega
mocks.w: This is Option writer margin. Option sellers must deposit margin because of their potential large losses; option buyers pay only the premium and need no margin.

mocks.p: A holder can exercise an option only on the last day. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: European option
Settlement of index options
Short call payoff
Put option buyer
mocks.w: This is European option. A European option can be exercised only on the expiry date. All options on Indian exchanges are European style.

mocks.p: A buffer on top of the SPAN margin for extra safety. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Exposure margin
Square off
Fair value of futures
Rollover
mocks.w: This is Exposure margin. Exposure margin is an additional margin over and above SPAN margin, collected to cover risk beyond that measured.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Gamma” is correct?
o: Gamma is the change in price for time decay.
Gamma measures how much delta changes for a ₹1 move in the underlying. It is highest for at-the-money options near expiry.
A call is in the money when spot is below the strike.
An at-the-money option has high intrinsic value.
mocks.w: Correct: Gamma measures how much delta changes for a ₹1 move in the underlying. It is highest for at-the-money options near expiry.

mocks.p: A margin system that assesses the worst-case scenario for the entire portfolio. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: SPAN
Futures versus forwards risk
Index futures
Cash settlement
mocks.w: This is SPAN. SPAN is a risk-based margining system that estimates the largest likely one-day loss across a portfolio under many scenarios.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Futures versus forwards risk” is correct?
o: Futures profits or losses are settled only at expiry.
SPAN charges a fixed 5% on every contract.
Forward contracts are guaranteed by the exchange.
Exchange-traded futures remove counterparty risk through the clearing corporation, while forwards leave it with the counterparty.
mocks.w: Correct: Exchange-traded futures remove counterparty risk through the clearing corporation, while forwards leave it with the counterparty.

mocks.p: An option's sensitivity to the interest rate. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Long put payoff
Option writer margin
Put option buyer
Rho
mocks.w: This is Rho. Rho measures the change in an option's price for a 1% change in the interest rate.

mocks.p: A broker that trades and clears by itself. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Self-clearing member
Clearing corporation
Settlement of premium
Peak margin
mocks.w: This is Self-clearing member. A self-clearing member is a trading member who also clears its own trades and its clients' trades.

mocks.p: A call buyer exercises and a writer is called to deliver. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Put option seller
Exercise and assignment
Short call payoff
Weekly options
mocks.w: This is Exercise and assignment. When a buyer exercises, a seller is assigned at random or by rule and must perform the obligation under the contract.

mocks.p: On the last day the future and spot are nearly equal. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Single-stock futures
Cash settlement
Convergence
Futures margin and leverage
mocks.w: This is Convergence. On the expiry date the futures price converges to the spot price of the underlying.

mocks.p: An entity always quotes both buy and sell prices to keep the market liquid. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Market-wide position limit
Order matching
Market maker
Client position limit
mocks.w: This is Market maker. A market maker quotes continuous two-way prices to provide liquidity in a contract.

mocks.p: A broker checks that a retail client understands leverage before allowing trades. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Suitability
Risk disclosure document
L.C. Gupta Committee
Investor Protection Fund
mocks.w: This is Suitability. Intermediaries must ensure that derivatives trading is suitable for the client given experience, income and risk appetite.

mocks.p: A trader receives ₹15 and must buy at ₹500 if the price collapses. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Put option seller
Call option buyer
Settlement of index options
Time value
mocks.w: This is Put option seller. The put seller receives the premium and must buy the underlying at the strike if exercised. Maximum profit is the premium; loss can be large if prices fall.

mocks.p: A firm that settles trades on behalf of other brokers with the clearing corporation. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Settlement of premium
Self-clearing member
Daily settlement price
Clearing member
mocks.w: This is Clearing member. A clearing member is authorised to clear and settle trades with the clearing corporation, for itself or for trading members.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Collateral for margin” is correct?
o: The daily settlement price is the opening price.
Margin can be given in cash, bank guarantees, fixed deposit receipts or approved securities, subject to haircuts.
Only cash is accepted as margin.
Margin is checked only at the market close.
mocks.w: Correct: Margin can be given in cash, bank guarantees, fixed deposit receipts or approved securities, subject to haircuts.

mocks.p: A contract's value moves with the price of a stock index. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Speculator
Derivative
Over-the-counter derivative
Underlying
mocks.w: This is Derivative. A derivative is a financial contract whose value depends on, or is derived from, an underlying asset or reference rate such as a share, index, currency or commodity.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Intermediaries must know the client's identity, financial position and investment objectives before allowing derivative trades.
o: Code of conduct
Complaint handling
Know your client
Conflict of interest
mocks.w: Know your client: Intermediaries must know the client's identity, financial position and investment objectives before allowing derivative trades.

mocks.p: An insider buys stock futures before the company announces a merger. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Risk disclosure document
Trading member
Prohibition of insider trading
Segregation of client funds
mocks.w: This is Prohibition of insider trading. Using unpublished price-sensitive information to trade stock derivatives is an offence under SEBI rules.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Arbitrageur” is correct?
o: A derivative is a share issued by a company.
An arbitrageur exploits price differences between related markets to earn a low-risk profit.
A forward contract is standardised and traded on exchanges.
An arbitrageur needs to predict the market's direction.
mocks.w: Correct: An arbitrageur exploits price differences between related markets to earn a low-risk profit.

mocks.p: A trader must hold margin for the highest exposure taken at any time in the day. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Professional clearing member
Peak margin
Haircut
Position squaring and exercise
mocks.w: This is Peak margin. Peak margin rules require traders to maintain margin at the highest level of exposure during the day, not just at the end of the day.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? OTC derivatives are privately negotiated and tailor-made but carry higher counterparty and liquidity risk.
o: Price discovery
Exchange-traded derivative
Over-the-counter derivative
Underlying
mocks.w: Over-the-counter derivative: OTC derivatives are privately negotiated and tailor-made but carry higher counterparty and liquidity risk.

mocks.p: A client of a failed broker receives compensation from the exchange fund. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: L.C. Gupta Committee
Grievance redressal and arbitration
Risk disclosure document
Investor Protection Fund
mocks.w: This is Investor Protection Fund. Exchanges maintain a fund to compensate clients of defaulting members within prescribed limits.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Contract specification” is correct?
o: An exchange fixes the underlying, lot size, tick size, expiry cycle and settlement method for each derivatives contract.
Stock futures are always cash settled.
Traders choose the lot size and expiry date themselves.
Rollover means taking physical delivery.
mocks.w: Correct: An exchange fixes the underlying, lot size, tick size, expiry cycle and settlement method for each derivatives contract.

mocks.p: A future at ₹2,000 with a lot of 500 has an exposure of ₹10 lakh. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Index futures
Contract value
Square off
Exposure margin
mocks.w: This is Contract value. Contract value equals futures price multiplied by the lot size and shows the exposure in rupees.

mocks.p: After matching, each side deals with the clearing corporation instead of the other party. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Novation
Default handling
Settlement of premium
Self-clearing member
mocks.w: This is Novation. Novation replaces the original contract between buyer and seller with two contracts, each with the clearing corporation as counterparty.

mocks.p: A defaulting member's deposits are used before other funds. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Haircut
Clearing corporation
Mark-to-market margin
Default handling
mocks.w: This is Default handling. On a member's default, the clearing corporation uses the member's margins and deposits first, then other resources, to complete settlement.

mocks.p: A call with strike 500 and spot 560 has a value of ₹60 on exercise. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Put option seller
European option
Intrinsic value
Rho
mocks.w: This is Intrinsic value. Intrinsic value is the amount by which an option is in the money, and is never negative. For a call it is the greater of (spot − strike) and zero.

mocks.p: Which statement about “J.R. Varma Committee” is correct?
o: The Varma committee recommended banning index futures.
The SCRA bans all derivatives trading.
Trading members need no certification.
The Prof. J. R. Varma Committee recommended risk containment measures, including margining systems, for derivatives trading.
mocks.w: Correct: The Prof. J. R. Varma Committee recommended risk containment measures, including margining systems, for derivatives trading.

mocks.p: A call with delta 0.5 gains about ₹0.50 if the underlying rises ₹1. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Put option buyer
Option chain
Option premium determinants
Delta
mocks.w: This is Delta. Delta measures the change in an option's price for a ₹1 change in the underlying. Calls have delta between 0 and 1; puts between −1 and 0.

mocks.p: A trader takes a view on the market as a whole with one contract. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Index futures
Fair value of futures
Futures versus forwards risk
SPAN
mocks.w: This is Index futures. Index futures are contracts on stock indices such as the Nifty 50, are cash settled, and are widely used to hedge and speculate on the overall market.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Contract value” is correct?
o: Contract value equals the margin.
Single-stock futures are available for any listed company.
Contract value equals futures price multiplied by the lot size and shows the exposure in rupees.
Backwardation means futures trade above spot.
mocks.w: Correct: Contract value equals futures price multiplied by the lot size and shows the exposure in rupees.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Position limits restrict the open positions a single client or member can hold, to prevent concentration and manipulation.
o: Price band in derivatives
Client position limit
Market maker
Order matching
mocks.w: Client position limit: Position limits restrict the open positions a single client or member can hold, to prevent concentration and manipulation.

mocks.p: A price can change only in steps of five paise. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Square off
Contract specification
Tick size
Single-stock futures
mocks.w: This is Tick size. The tick size is the minimum price movement allowed for a contract, such as ₹0.05 for futures on equity.

mocks.p: A person expecting to buy shares next month buys futures to lock in prices. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Long futures position
Long hedge versus short hedge
Convergence
Contract value
mocks.w: This is Long hedge versus short hedge. A short hedge sells futures to protect against price falls; a long hedge buys futures to protect against price rises.

mocks.p: The law that defines securities and allows derivatives trading on recognised exchanges. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Trading member
SCRA
L.C. Gupta Committee
Minimum contract size
mocks.w: This is SCRA. The Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 regulates trading in securities and, after amendment, recognises derivatives as securities.

mocks.p: Spot is 24,000 and the future is 24,060; the gap shrinks as expiry nears. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Index futures
Expiry cycle
Basis
Mark-to-market
mocks.w: This is Basis. Basis is the difference between the spot price and the futures price. It narrows to zero at expiry as the two prices converge.

mocks.p: A broker holds client money in a separate account. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: SEBI Act
Certification requirement
Contract note
Segregation of client funds
mocks.w: This is Segregation of client funds. Brokers must keep client funds and securities separate from their own and must not use them for proprietary trading.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Rolling over means closing a near-month position and opening a similar position in the next month to maintain exposure.
o: Expiry cycle
Rollover
Initial margin
SPAN
mocks.w: Rollover: Rolling over means closing a near-month position and opening a similar position in the next month to maintain exposure.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Extreme loss margin” is correct?
o: Positions cannot be closed before expiry.
Extreme loss margin is the same as premium.
MTM margin is collected only at expiry.
Extreme loss margin covers losses beyond those captured by SPAN in highly adverse moves.
mocks.w: Correct: Extreme loss margin covers losses beyond those captured by SPAN in highly adverse moves.

mocks.p: A call with strike 500 when spot is 550. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: In-the-money
Time value
Option premium determinants
Short put payoff
mocks.w: This is In-the-money. A call is in the money when spot is above the strike; a put is in the money when spot is below the strike. It has positive intrinsic value.

mocks.p: A sales trader must hold the examination certificate to deal. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Certification requirement
J.R. Varma Committee
Segregation of client funds
Suitability
mocks.w: This is Certification requirement. Dealers and persons who handle derivatives business must pass the NISM derivatives certification examination.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Weekly options” is correct?
o: Exchanges list options with weekly expiries on selected indices, subject to regulatory limits on the number of contracts.
All stock options expire weekly.
An American option can be exercised only at expiry.
Stock options are always cash settled.
mocks.w: Correct: Exchanges list options with weekly expiries on selected indices, subject to regulatory limits on the number of contracts.

mocks.p: A client receives a document confirming the details of her trade. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Risk disclosure document
Prohibition of insider trading
Surveillance
Contract note
mocks.w: This is Contract note. A broker must issue a contract note for every trade, showing price, time, brokerage and charges, usually within 24 hours.

mocks.p: A futures contract is based on the Nifty 50, which is its reference. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Leverage
Speculator
Underlying
Forward contract
mocks.w: This is Underlying. The underlying is the asset or index on which a derivative contract is based.

mocks.p: A table showing calls on one side and puts on the other by strike price. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Implied volatility
Option chain
Gamma
Delta
mocks.w: This is Option chain. An option chain lists the available strikes and premiums of calls and puts for a given underlying and expiry.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Settlement guarantee fund” is correct?
o: Only cash is accepted as margin.
The clearing corporation maintains a fund to cover member defaults, built from contributions of members and the corporation.
A haircut increases the collateral value.
The fund is paid to investors as dividend.
mocks.w: Correct: The clearing corporation maintains a fund to cover member defaults, built from contributions of members and the corporation.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? The call seller (writer) receives the premium and must sell the underlying at the strike if exercised. The maximum profit is the premium and the loss is potentially unlimited.
o: Long call payoff
In-the-money
Call option seller
Exercise and assignment
mocks.w: Call option seller: The call seller (writer) receives the premium and must sell the underlying at the strike if exercised. The maximum profit is the premium and the loss is potentially unlimited.

mocks.p: Turnover is computed by adding absolute profits and losses for futures. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Mark-to-market accounting
Turnover for derivatives
Carry forward of business losses
Tax audit
mocks.w: This is Turnover for derivatives. For tax audit purposes, turnover of futures and options is computed using specified methods, such as the absolute profit and loss and premium on sale of options.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Trading member” is correct?
o: Trading members need no certification.
Anyone can deal in derivatives without certification.
The SCRA bans all derivatives trading.
A trading member of the derivatives segment must be registered with SEBI, meet net-worth and certification norms, and have qualified dealers.
mocks.w: Correct: A trading member of the derivatives segment must be registered with SEBI, meet net-worth and certification norms, and have qualified dealers.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Forward contract” is correct?
o: A swap is an exchange-traded futures contract.
A hedger aims to maximise profit from price moves.
A forward contract is a private agreement to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price on a future date. It is customised and traded over the counter, with counterparty risk.
A forward contract is standardised and traded on exchanges.
mocks.w: Correct: A forward contract is a private agreement to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price on a future date. It is customised and traded over the counter, with counterparty risk.

mocks.p: An option on a very volatile stock costs more than one on a stable stock. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Option chain
Implied volatility
Option premium determinants
Long call payoff
mocks.w: This is Option premium determinants. The premium depends on spot, strike, time to expiry, volatility, interest rates and dividends; higher volatility and longer time raise it.

mocks.p: An index future ends with a rupee payment, not with shares. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Contract value
Contango
Convergence
Cash settlement
mocks.w: This is Cash settlement. In cash settlement, no underlying is delivered; the difference between the contract price and the settlement price is paid in cash.

mocks.p: A trader buys an index future at 24,000 and it moves to 24,100. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Long futures position
Tick size
Expiry cycle
Square off
mocks.w: This is Long futures position. A long futures position buys the contract and gains when the price rises above the entry price and loses when it falls.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? SEBI prescribes a minimum value for a derivatives contract at the time of its introduction, reviewed periodically, so that lot sizes are meaningful.
o: Eligibility of stocks
Surveillance
Proprietary versus client trades
Minimum contract size
mocks.w: Minimum contract size: SEBI prescribes a minimum value for a derivatives contract at the time of its introduction, reviewed periodically, so that lot sizes are meaningful.

mocks.p: A trader expects a big move after results but not its direction. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Bull call spread
Butterfly spread
Long straddle
Long strangle
mocks.w: This is Long straddle. A long straddle buys a call and a put at the same strike and expiry, profiting from a large move in either direction.

mocks.p: Three monthly contracts are available at any time. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Backwardation
SPAN
Expiry cycle
Physical settlement
mocks.w: This is Expiry cycle. Index and stock futures have near-month, next-month and far-month contracts, and a contract expires on the day set by the exchange; on expiry it is cash settled.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Speculator” is correct?
o: An arbitrageur needs to predict the market's direction.
A speculator takes positions in derivatives to profit from expected price changes and accepts the risk.
A speculator has no exposure to the price risk.
Exchange-traded derivatives are customised for each buyer.
mocks.w: Correct: A speculator takes positions in derivatives to profit from expected price changes and accepts the risk.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Long put payoff” is correct?
o: An at-the-money option has high intrinsic value.
Option buyers must deposit margin like sellers.
A long put's break-even is strike plus premium.
A long put's profit at expiry = max(strike − spot, 0) − premium; break-even = strike − premium.
mocks.w: Correct: A long put's profit at expiry = max(strike − spot, 0) − premium; break-even = strike − premium.

mocks.p: Which term is described here? Free-float market capitalisation weighting weights each stock by the value of shares available for public trading, so promoter holdings are excluded.
o: Base value
Stock index
Free-float weighting
Beta of a portfolio
mocks.w: Free-float weighting: Free-float market capitalisation weighting weights each stock by the value of shares available for public trading, so promoter holdings are excluded.

mocks.p: A trader pays ₹15 for the right to sell at ₹500 and expects a fall. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Put option seller
Implied volatility
At-the-money
Put option buyer
mocks.w: This is Put option buyer. The buyer of a put pays a premium and has the right to sell at the strike. Maximum loss is the premium; profit rises as the price falls to zero.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Initial margin is refunded as profit after the first day.
Index futures are contracts on stock indices such as the Nifty 50, are cash settled, and are widely used to hedge and speculate on the overall market.
Because only margin is paid upfront, futures offer leverage: a small price change can produce a large percentage gain or loss on margin.
In physical settlement, the underlying shares are actually delivered on expiry; stock derivatives in India are physically settled.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Initial margin is the upfront deposit collected to cover the potential loss on a futures position over a short period. It is risk-based, using the SPAN system.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Peak margin rules require traders to maintain margin at the highest level of exposure during the day, not just at the end of the day.
MTM margin is collected from members for the day's losses on open positions, to ensure daily settlement.
The clearing corporation sets prices of contracts.
A self-clearing member is a trading member who also clears its own trades and its clients' trades.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The clearing corporation becomes the counterparty to every trade through novation, guaranteeing settlement and managing risk.

mocks.p: An in-the-money index option ends with a cash credit. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Time value
Intrinsic value
In-the-money
Settlement of index options
mocks.w: This is Settlement of index options. Index options are cash settled at expiry on the closing index value; in-the-money options are exercised automatically.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Contango” is correct?
o: Contango means futures trade below spot.
Futures margin limits the loss to the margin amount.
Contango is a market in which futures prices are higher than the spot price, normally due to carrying costs.
Futures profits or losses are settled only at expiry.
mocks.w: Correct: Contango is a market in which futures prices are higher than the spot price, normally due to carrying costs.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Exchange-traded futures remove counterparty risk through the clearing corporation, while forwards leave it with the counterparty.
Cash-and-carry arbitrage buys futures and sells shares.
Backwardation is a market in which futures prices are lower than the spot price.
Initial margin is the upfront deposit collected to cover the potential loss on a futures position over a short period. It is risk-based, using the SPAN system.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Cash-and-carry arbitrage buys the underlying in the cash market and sells the future when the future is expensive relative to fair value.

mocks.p: A trader whose position fell during the day pays the difference. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Daily settlement price
Mark-to-market margin
Position squaring and exercise
Peak margin
mocks.w: This is Mark-to-market margin. MTM margin is collected from members for the day's losses on open positions, to ensure daily settlement.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The daily settlement price of futures is generally the closing price (average of the last half hour), and positions are marked against it.
The clearing corporation maintains a fund to cover member defaults, built from contributions of members and the corporation.
The clearing corporation becomes the counterparty to every trade through novation, guaranteeing settlement and managing risk.
A haircut increases the collateral value.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A haircut is a reduction applied to the value of collateral securities to protect against price falls.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Initial margin is the upfront deposit collected to cover the potential loss on a futures position over a short period. It is risk-based, using the SPAN system.
Index and stock futures have near-month, next-month and far-month contracts, and a contract expires on the day set by the exchange; on expiry it is cash settled.
Reverse cash-and-carry buys the underlying and sells futures.
Rolling over means closing a near-month position and opening a similar position in the next month to maintain exposure.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Reverse cash-and-carry sells the underlying and buys the future when the future is cheap relative to fair value.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Segregation of client funds” is correct?
o: The SEBI Act regulates only banks.
Brokers must keep client funds and securities separate from their own and must not use them for proprietary trading.
Brokers may use client funds for their own trades.
Trading members need no certification.
mocks.w: Correct: Brokers must keep client funds and securities separate from their own and must not use them for proprietary trading.

mocks.p: After a trade, the buyer's counterparty is the clearing entity, not the seller. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Self-clearing member
Extreme loss margin
Haircut
Clearing corporation
mocks.w: This is Clearing corporation. The clearing corporation becomes the counterparty to every trade through novation, guaranteeing settlement and managing risk.

mocks.p: Open positions are valued at the closing price on the balance sheet date. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Mark-to-market accounting
Non-speculative business income
Carry forward of business losses
Tax audit
mocks.w: This is Mark-to-market accounting. Open futures positions are marked to market at year end for accounting, and unrealised losses may be recognised.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Intermediaries must ensure that derivatives trading is suitable for the client given experience, income and risk appetite.
Brokers must distinguish their own proprietary trades from client trades and ensure they are reported and handled separately.
Insider trading rules apply only to shares and not to derivatives.
Brokers must keep client funds and securities separate from their own and must not use them for proprietary trading.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Using unpublished price-sensitive information to trade stock derivatives is an offence under SEBI rules.

mocks.p: A stock's derivative position exceeds 95% of the limit and is banned for fresh positions. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Market-wide position limit
Trading hours of derivatives
Order types
Client position limit
mocks.w: This is Market-wide position limit. The MWPL caps the total open positions across all traders in a stock's derivatives; when it reaches 95% the stock enters a ban period.

mocks.p: A trader who bought a future sells the same contract to close the position. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Contract value
Mark-to-market
Square off
Index futures
mocks.w: This is Square off. Squaring off means closing an open position by taking an equal and opposite position in the same contract before expiry.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A long futures position buys the contract and gains when the price rises above the entry price and loses when it falls.
SPAN is a risk-based margining system that estimates the largest likely one-day loss across a portfolio under many scenarios.
Futures can trade at any price without arbitrage.
Backwardation is a market in which futures prices are lower than the spot price.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The fair price of a futures contract is the spot price plus the net cost of carry; deviations create arbitrage opportunities.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The Dr. L. C. Gupta Committee (1998) recommended the introduction of derivatives trading in India and laid out the regulatory framework.
Brokers must keep client funds and securities separate from their own and must not use them for proprietary trading.
The Varma committee recommended banning index futures.
Stocks are admitted to derivatives based on criteria such as market capitalisation, free float, trading frequency and volatility.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The Prof. J. R. Varma Committee recommended risk containment measures, including margining systems, for derivatives trading.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Option premium is settled in cash on T+1; the buyer pays and the seller receives.
The final settlement price is the previous month's average.
Novation replaces the original contract between buyer and seller with two contracts, each with the clearing corporation as counterparty.
Margin can be given in cash, bank guarantees, fixed deposit receipts or approved securities, subject to haircuts.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: On expiry, the final settlement price of index futures is the closing value of the underlying index.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Peak margin” is correct?
o: Margin is checked only at the market close.
Novation cancels the trade.
The clearing corporation sets prices of contracts.
Peak margin rules require traders to maintain margin at the highest level of exposure during the day, not just at the end of the day.
mocks.w: Correct: Peak margin rules require traders to maintain margin at the highest level of exposure during the day, not just at the end of the day.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Gamma measures how much delta changes for a ₹1 move in the underlying. It is highest for at-the-money options near expiry.
A call is in the money when spot is above the strike; a put is in the money when spot is below the strike. It has positive intrinsic value.
Vega measures the effect of interest rate changes.
A long put's profit at expiry = max(strike − spot, 0) − premium; break-even = strike − premium.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Vega measures the change in an option's price for a 1% change in volatility. Higher volatility raises both call and put prices.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Contract value equals futures price multiplied by the lot size and shows the exposure in rupees.
A short hedge sells futures to protect against price falls; a long hedge buys futures to protect against price rises.
Squaring off means closing an open position by taking an equal and opposite position in the same contract before expiry.
Exposure margin replaces SPAN margin entirely.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Exposure margin is an additional margin over and above SPAN margin, collected to cover risk beyond that measured.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Over-the-counter derivative” is correct?
o: OTC derivatives are privately negotiated and tailor-made but carry higher counterparty and liquidity risk.
A hedger aims to maximise profit from price moves.
Derivatives play no role in price discovery.
OTC derivatives are guaranteed by a clearing corporation.
mocks.w: Correct: OTC derivatives are privately negotiated and tailor-made but carry higher counterparty and liquidity risk.

mocks.p: A call with strike 500 bought at ₹20 breaks even at 520. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Call option seller
Long call payoff
Call option buyer
Settlement of stock options
mocks.w: This is Long call payoff. A long call's profit at expiry = max(spot − strike, 0) − premium; break-even = strike + premium.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Option writer margin” is correct?
o: The option buyer is always obliged to exercise.
Gamma is the change in price for time decay.
Option sellers must deposit margin because of their potential large losses; option buyers pay only the premium and need no margin.
Option buyers must deposit margin like sellers.
mocks.w: Correct: Option sellers must deposit margin because of their potential large losses; option buyers pay only the premium and need no margin.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: On a member's default, the clearing corporation uses the member's margins and deposits first, then other resources, to complete settlement.
A self-clearing member is a trading member who also clears its own trades and its clients' trades.
MTM margin is collected only at expiry.
Peak margin rules require traders to maintain margin at the highest level of exposure during the day, not just at the end of the day.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: MTM margin is collected from members for the day's losses on open positions, to ensure daily settlement.

mocks.p: A call buyer who is in the money at expiry gets shares delivered. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Intrinsic value
Put option seller
Settlement of stock options
Put option buyer
mocks.w: This is Settlement of stock options. Stock options are physically settled; in-the-money stock options at expiry result in delivery of shares.

mocks.p: Which statement about “At-the-money” is correct?
o: An at-the-money option has high intrinsic value.
A put buyer benefits when the price rises.
Theta helps option buyers.
An option is at the money when the strike equals the spot price. Its intrinsic value is zero.
mocks.w: Correct: An option is at the money when the strike equals the spot price. Its intrinsic value is zero.

mocks.p: A trader places a futures order at 10 am on a working day. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Trading hours of derivatives
Price band in derivatives
Market maker
Order types
mocks.w: This is Trading hours of derivatives. The equity derivatives segment trades during regular market hours, 9:15 am to 3:30 pm, on business days.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Exchanges and SEBI monitor derivatives markets for manipulation, with measures such as position limits and bans.
Clients have no recourse for disputes.
Brokers must give clients a risk disclosure document explaining the risks of derivatives, including leverage and the possibility of losing the entire margin.
A trading member of the derivatives segment must be registered with SEBI, meet net-worth and certification norms, and have qualified dealers.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Disputes between clients and brokers can be taken to the exchange's arbitration, investor service cells and SEBI's complaint system.

mocks.p: An option's price rises when volatility increases. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Vega
Early exercise of European options
Call option buyer
At-the-money
mocks.w: This is Vega. Vega measures the change in an option's price for a 1% change in volatility. Higher volatility raises both call and put prices.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The Prof. J. R. Varma Committee recommended risk containment measures, including margining systems, for derivatives trading.
Disputes between clients and brokers can be taken to the exchange's arbitration, investor service cells and SEBI's complaint system.
Exchanges maintain a fund to compensate clients of defaulting members within prescribed limits.
A client can trade before completing KYC.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Clients must complete KYC and sign a client-broker agreement before trading derivatives.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Because European options cannot be exercised early, holders who want to exit before expiry sell the option in the market.
A European option can be exercised any time before expiry.
Exchanges list options with weekly expiries on selected indices, subject to regulatory limits on the number of contracts.
An American option can be exercised at any time up to and including expiry.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A European option can be exercised only on the expiry date. All options on Indian exchanges are European style.

mocks.p: A committee whose report shaped margin and risk measures. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: J.R. Varma Committee
Certification requirement
Eligibility of stocks
Client registration
mocks.w: This is J.R. Varma Committee. The Prof. J. R. Varma Committee recommended risk containment measures, including margining systems, for derivatives trading.

mocks.p: A trader buys a 520 call and a 480 put. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Butterfly spread
Collar
Bear put spread
Long strangle
mocks.w: This is Long strangle. A long strangle buys an out-of-the-money call and an out-of-the-money put, costing less than a straddle but needing a bigger move.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Backwardation is a market in which futures prices are lower than the spot price.
Basis widens to its maximum at expiry.
SPAN is a risk-based margining system that estimates the largest likely one-day loss across a portfolio under many scenarios.
Cash-and-carry arbitrage buys the underlying in the cash market and sells the future when the future is expensive relative to fair value.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Basis is the difference between the spot price and the futures price. It narrows to zero at expiry as the two prices converge.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The exchange can fix any tiny contract value.
The Prof. J. R. Varma Committee recommended risk containment measures, including margining systems, for derivatives trading.
A trading member of the derivatives segment must be registered with SEBI, meet net-worth and certification norms, and have qualified dealers.
Exchanges maintain a fund to compensate clients of defaulting members within prescribed limits.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: SEBI prescribes a minimum value for a derivatives contract at the time of its introduction, reviewed periodically, so that lot sizes are meaningful.

mocks.p: A trader pays ₹20 for the right to buy at ₹500 and expects a rise. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Long put payoff
At-the-money
Call option buyer
Early exercise of European options
mocks.w: This is Call option buyer. The buyer of a call pays a premium and has the right to buy the underlying at the strike. Maximum loss is the premium and the potential profit is unlimited.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A clearing member is authorised to clear and settle trades with the clearing corporation, for itself or for trading members.
Novation replaces the original contract between buyer and seller with two contracts, each with the clearing corporation as counterparty.
A professional clearing member clears trades for others without being a trading member itself.
The investors' funds are used first for member defaults.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: On a member's default, the clearing corporation uses the member's margins and deposits first, then other resources, to complete settlement.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A trading member of the derivatives segment must be registered with SEBI, meet net-worth and certification norms, and have qualified dealers.
Stocks are admitted to derivatives based on criteria such as market capitalisation, free float, trading frequency and volatility.
The Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 regulates trading in securities and, after amendment, recognises derivatives as securities.
Brokers may use client funds for their own trades.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Brokers must keep client funds and securities separate from their own and must not use them for proprietary trading.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A pair trade is a single long position.
Basis is the difference between the spot price and the futures price. It narrows to zero at expiry as the two prices converge.
On the expiry date the futures price converges to the spot price of the underlying.
Because only margin is paid upfront, futures offer leverage: a small price change can produce a large percentage gain or loss on margin.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A pair trade buys one related security and sells another, profiting from relative price movement rather than market direction.

mocks.p: A client files a complaint and seeks arbitration against a broker. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Surveillance
Grievance redressal and arbitration
SEBI Act
Segregation of client funds
mocks.w: This is Grievance redressal and arbitration. Disputes between clients and brokers can be taken to the exchange's arbitration, investor service cells and SEBI's complaint system.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A protective put adds to the loss when prices fall.
A long strangle buys an out-of-the-money call and an out-of-the-money put, costing less than a straddle but needing a bigger move.
A covered call holds the underlying and sells a call against it, earning the premium but capping the upside.
A collar holds the underlying, buys a put and sells a call, limiting both downside and upside, often at a low net cost.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A protective put buys a put against a held position, setting a floor under the loss at the cost of the premium.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Short futures position” is correct?
o: Rollover means taking physical delivery.
Initial margin is refunded as profit after the first day.
A short futures position loses when the price falls.
A short position sells the contract and gains when the price falls below the entry price and loses when it rises.
mocks.w: Correct: A short position sells the contract and gains when the price falls below the entry price and loses when it rises.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An at-the-money option has high intrinsic value.
A European option can be exercised only on the expiry date. All options on Indian exchanges are European style.
Index options are cash settled at expiry on the closing index value; in-the-money options are exercised automatically.
A call is in the money when spot is above the strike; a put is in the money when spot is below the strike. It has positive intrinsic value.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: An option is at the money when the strike equals the spot price. Its intrinsic value is zero.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Using unpublished price-sensitive information to trade stock derivatives is an offence under SEBI rules.
Proprietary and client trades are mixed together.
The SEBI Act, 1992 gives SEBI the power to regulate the securities market, including derivatives, and protect investors.
Exchanges maintain a fund to compensate clients of defaulting members within prescribed limits.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Brokers must distinguish their own proprietary trades from client trades and ensure they are reported and handled separately.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Long futures position” is correct?
o: Stock futures are always cash settled.
A long futures position buys the contract and gains when the price rises above the entry price and loses when it falls.
Cash-and-carry arbitrage buys futures and sells shares.
A long futures position gains when the price falls.
mocks.w: Correct: A long futures position buys the contract and gains when the price rises above the entry price and loses when it falls.

mocks.p: A clearing corporation guarantees that the futures trade will be honoured. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Square off
Futures versus forwards risk
Index futures
Convergence
mocks.w: This is Futures versus forwards risk. Exchange-traded futures remove counterparty risk through the clearing corporation, while forwards leave it with the counterparty.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An out-of-the-money option has the highest intrinsic value.
Stock options are physically settled; in-the-money stock options at expiry result in delivery of shares.
Exchanges list options with weekly expiries on selected indices, subject to regulatory limits on the number of contracts.
An option is at the money when the strike equals the spot price. Its intrinsic value is zero.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A call is out of the money when spot is below the strike; a put when spot is above the strike. It has no intrinsic value, only time value.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Price band in derivatives” is correct?
o: A market maker only buys, never sells.
Derivatives have operating ranges that stop orders far from the last price, to prevent erroneous trades.
There is no price protection in derivatives.
Equity derivatives trade only in the pre-open session.
mocks.w: Correct: Derivatives have operating ranges that stop orders far from the last price, to prevent erroneous trades.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Option premium determinants” is correct?
o: The premium depends on spot, strike, time to expiry, volatility, interest rates and dividends; higher volatility and longer time raise it.
Volatility has no effect on option premium.
Vega measures the effect of interest rate changes.
A European option can be exercised any time before expiry.
mocks.w: Correct: The premium depends on spot, strike, time to expiry, volatility, interest rates and dividends; higher volatility and longer time raise it.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The fair price of a futures contract is the spot price plus the net cost of carry; deviations create arbitrage opportunities.
A short position sells the contract and gains when the price falls below the entry price and loses when it rises.
Traders choose the lot size and expiry date themselves.
Backwardation is a market in which futures prices are lower than the spot price.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: An exchange fixes the underlying, lot size, tick size, expiry cycle and settlement method for each derivatives contract.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: SEBI prescribes a minimum value for a derivatives contract at the time of its introduction, reviewed periodically, so that lot sizes are meaningful.
The Prof. J. R. Varma Committee recommended risk containment measures, including margining systems, for derivatives trading.
Anyone can deal in derivatives without certification.
The Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956 regulates trading in securities and, after amendment, recognises derivatives as securities.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Dealers and persons who handle derivatives business must pass the NISM derivatives certification examination.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Beta measures the dividend of a stock.
A stock index is a number measuring the combined price performance of a basket of stocks, used as a market barometer and as the underlying of index derivatives.
Index constituents are reviewed periodically and stocks replaced when they no longer meet criteria on market cap, liquidity and free float.
An index starts at a base value on a base date; the Nifty 50 base is 1000 and the Sensex base is 100, and later values are relative to them.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Beta measures the sensitivity of a portfolio to market moves; a beta of 1.2 means it is expected to move 20% more than the index.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A swap is an agreement to exchange cash flows over a period, such as fixed for floating interest payments.
A forward contract is standardised and traded on exchanges.
An arbitrageur exploits price differences between related markets to earn a low-risk profit.
Exchange-traded derivatives have standardised terms, are cleared by a clearing corporation and carry lower counterparty risk.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A forward contract is a private agreement to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price on a future date. It is customised and traded over the counter, with counterparty risk.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An arbitrageur exploits price differences between related markets to earn a low-risk profit.
A hedger aims to maximise profit from price moves.
Derivatives markets help in price discovery by reflecting market expectations about future prices of the underlying.
A speculator takes positions in derivatives to profit from expected price changes and accepts the risk.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A hedger uses derivatives to reduce an existing price risk rather than to profit from price moves.

mocks.p: A stock future held to expiry results in delivery of shares. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Hedging with index futures
Cost of carry
Physical settlement
Long hedge versus short hedge
mocks.w: This is Physical settlement. In physical settlement, the underlying shares are actually delivered on expiry; stock derivatives in India are physically settled.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Basis is the difference between the spot price and the futures price. It narrows to zero at expiry as the two prices converge.
Because only margin is paid upfront, futures offer leverage: a small price change can produce a large percentage gain or loss on margin.
Index futures are contracts on stock indices such as the Nifty 50, are cash settled, and are widely used to hedge and speculate on the overall market.
Squaring off means doubling a position.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Squaring off means closing an open position by taking an equal and opposite position in the same contract before expiry.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Derivatives have operating ranges that stop orders far from the last price, to prevent erroneous trades.
During a ban period all trading is banned.
Orders on the exchange are matched on price-time priority: the best price first, and among equal prices the earliest order.
The MWPL caps the total open positions across all traders in a stock's derivatives; when it reaches 95% the stock enters a ban period.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: In the ban period, traders can only reduce their open positions in the stock; fresh positions are not allowed.

mocks.p: The premium for an option traded today is settled the following business day. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Early exercise of European options
Premium settlement
Put-call parity
Call option buyer
mocks.w: This is Premium settlement. Premium is paid by the buyer and received by the seller on the next working day after the trade.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Short put payoff” is correct?
o: An option chain shows only futures prices.
A short put's profit at expiry = premium − max(strike − spot, 0); break-even = strike − premium.
A short put is profitable at any fall in price.
A short call is profitable at any rise in price.
mocks.w: Correct: A short put's profit at expiry = premium − max(strike − spot, 0); break-even = strike − premium.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: An American option can be exercised at any time up to and including expiry.
A call is in the money when spot is above the strike; a put is in the money when spot is below the strike. It has positive intrinsic value.
A long put's break-even is strike plus premium.
Vega measures the change in an option's price for a 1% change in volatility. Higher volatility raises both call and put prices.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A long put's profit at expiry = max(strike − spot, 0) − premium; break-even = strike − premium.

mocks.p: A trader pledges approved shares instead of cash margin. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Settlement of premium
Settlement guarantee fund
Collateral for margin
Mark-to-market margin
mocks.w: This is Collateral for margin. Margin can be given in cash, bank guarantees, fixed deposit receipts or approved securities, subject to haircuts.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: On a member's default, the clearing corporation uses the member's margins and deposits first, then other resources, to complete settlement.
Option premium is settled in cash on T+1; the buyer pays and the seller receives.
Extreme loss margin is the same as premium.
A position can be closed by an opposite trade or held to expiry, when options are exercised or lapse and futures are settled.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Extreme loss margin covers losses beyond those captured by SPAN in highly adverse moves.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Gamma measures how much delta changes for a ₹1 move in the underlying. It is highest for at-the-money options near expiry.
Premium is paid by the buyer and received by the seller on the next working day after the trade.
A call buyer has unlimited loss.
A European option can be exercised only on the expiry date. All options on Indian exchanges are European style.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The buyer of a call pays a premium and has the right to buy the underlying at the strike. Maximum loss is the premium and the potential profit is unlimited.

mocks.p: A writer who sold a 500 call at ₹20 starts losing above 520. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Weekly options
Short call payoff
Gamma
Long call payoff
mocks.w: This is Short call payoff. A short call's profit at expiry = premium − max(spot − strike, 0); break-even = strike + premium.

mocks.p: A committee that paved the way for derivatives in India. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: L.C. Gupta Committee
Investor Protection Fund
Minimum contract size
Client registration
mocks.w: This is L.C. Gupta Committee. The Dr. L. C. Gupta Committee (1998) recommended the introduction of derivatives trading in India and laid out the regulatory framework.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Because only margin is paid upfront, futures offer leverage: a small price change can produce a large percentage gain or loss on margin.
SPAN is a risk-based margining system that estimates the largest likely one-day loss across a portfolio under many scenarios.
A short futures position loses when the price falls.
Index futures are contracts on stock indices such as the Nifty 50, are cash settled, and are widely used to hedge and speculate on the overall market.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A short position sells the contract and gains when the price falls below the entry price and loses when it rises.

mocks.p: Two parties agree to exchange a fixed rate payment for a floating one. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Swap
Speculator
Exchange-traded derivative
Futures contract
mocks.w: This is Swap. A swap is an agreement to exchange cash flows over a period, such as fixed for floating interest payments.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A swap is an agreement to exchange cash flows over a period, such as fixed for floating interest payments.
Leverage in derivatives means controlling a large exposure with a small margin, magnifying both gains and losses.
The underlying is the premium paid on an option.
A forward contract is a private agreement to buy or sell an asset at a fixed price on a future date. It is customised and traded over the counter, with counterparty risk.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The underlying is the asset or index on which a derivative contract is based.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Initial margin is the upfront deposit collected to cover the potential loss on a futures position over a short period. It is risk-based, using the SPAN system.
A short hedge sells futures to protect against price falls; a long hedge buys futures to protect against price rises.
A long futures position gains when the price falls.
Open interest is the total number of outstanding contracts not yet squared off or settled, showing how many positions remain open.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A long futures position buys the contract and gains when the price rises above the entry price and loses when it falls.

mocks.p: The price used to compute each day's profit or loss on futures. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Daily settlement price
Mark-to-market margin
Clearing corporation
Position squaring and exercise
mocks.w: This is Daily settlement price. The daily settlement price of futures is generally the closing price (average of the last half hour), and positions are marked against it.

mocks.p: A trader's F&O loss is carried forward to future years. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Mark-to-market accounting
Turnover for derivatives
Carry forward of business losses
Tax audit
mocks.w: This is Carry forward of business losses. Non-speculative business losses from derivatives can be set off against other business income and carried forward for eight years if returns are filed on time.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A clearing member is authorised to clear and settle trades with the clearing corporation, for itself or for trading members.
The fund is paid to investors as dividend.
On expiry, the final settlement price of index futures is the closing value of the underlying index.
A professional clearing member clears trades for others without being a trading member itself.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: The clearing corporation maintains a fund to cover member defaults, built from contributions of members and the corporation.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Collar” is correct?
o: A collar holds the underlying, buys a put and sells a call, limiting both downside and upside, often at a low net cost.
A long straddle profits if the price stays still.
A collar leaves both ends of risk unlimited.
A protective put adds to the loss when prices fall.
mocks.w: Correct: A collar holds the underlying, buys a put and sells a call, limiting both downside and upside, often at a low net cost.

mocks.p: A dealer explains that a short option can lose more than the premium collected. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Appropriate advice
Code of conduct
Complaint handling
Know your client
mocks.w: This is Appropriate advice. Dealers should explain leverage, margin calls and potential loss and avoid pushing high-risk strategies to unsuitable clients.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Exchange-traded futures remove counterparty risk through the clearing corporation, while forwards leave it with the counterparty.
Futures and spot are unrelated at expiry.
A portfolio owner can sell index futures to protect against a fall in the market; the number of contracts depends on portfolio value and beta.
A long futures position buys the contract and gains when the price rises above the entry price and loses when it falls.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: On the expiry date the futures price converges to the spot price of the underlying.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A long put's profit at expiry = max(strike − spot, 0) − premium; break-even = strike − premium.
Because European options cannot be exercised early, holders who want to exit before expiry sell the option in the market.
A call is in the money when spot is below the strike.
Index options are cash settled at expiry on the closing index value; in-the-money options are exercised automatically.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: A call is in the money when spot is above the strike; a put is in the money when spot is below the strike. It has positive intrinsic value.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Index futures are delivered in shares.
A long futures position buys the contract and gains when the price rises above the entry price and loses when it falls.
Squaring off means closing an open position by taking an equal and opposite position in the same contract before expiry.
Index and stock futures have near-month, next-month and far-month contracts, and a contract expires on the day set by the exchange; on expiry it is cash settled.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Index futures are contracts on stock indices such as the Nifty 50, are cash settled, and are widely used to hedge and speculate on the overall market.

mocks.p: A holder sells the option in the market a week before expiry. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Call option seller
Early exercise of European options
Option premium determinants
European option
mocks.w: This is Early exercise of European options. Because European options cannot be exercised early, holders who want to exit before expiry sell the option in the market.

mocks.p: A future trades at a discount to the spot price. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Backwardation
Hedging with index futures
SPAN
Mark-to-market
mocks.w: This is Backwardation. Backwardation is a market in which futures prices are lower than the spot price.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Reverse cash-and-carry sells the underlying and buys the future when the future is cheap relative to fair value.
Index futures are contracts on stock indices such as the Nifty 50, are cash settled, and are widely used to hedge and speculate on the overall market.
The cost of carry is the cost of holding the underlying until expiry, mainly financing cost less any income such as dividends, and drives futures pricing.
Single-stock futures are available for any listed company.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Single stock futures are futures on individual shares, available for eligible stocks with liquidity and market-cap criteria.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Brokers must keep client funds and securities separate from their own and must not use them for proprietary trading.
SEBI prescribes a minimum value for a derivatives contract at the time of its introduction, reviewed periodically, so that lot sizes are meaningful.
A broker must issue a contract note for every trade, showing price, time, brokerage and charges, usually within 24 hours.
Suitability is irrelevant to broking.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Intermediaries must ensure that derivatives trading is suitable for the client given experience, income and risk appetite.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Code of conduct” is correct?
o: Brokers can guarantee returns in derivatives.
Front running is permitted if the client is not aware.
Clients can complain only after a year.
A code of conduct for brokers requires honesty, fairness, due diligence and prohibits misleading statements and unfair practices.
mocks.w: Correct: A code of conduct for brokers requires honesty, fairness, due diligence and prohibits misleading statements and unfair practices.

mocks.p: A trader receives ₹20 and must sell if the price rises sharply. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Put option seller
Implied volatility
American option
Call option seller
mocks.w: This is Call option seller. The call seller (writer) receives the premium and must sell the underlying at the strike if exercised. The maximum profit is the premium and the loss is potentially unlimited.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Final settlement price” is correct?
o: Positions cannot be closed before expiry.
On expiry, the final settlement price of index futures is the closing value of the underlying index.
Novation cancels the trade.
The final settlement price is the previous month's average.
mocks.w: Correct: On expiry, the final settlement price of index futures is the closing value of the underlying index.

mocks.p: A contract lot is set to meet the regulator's minimum value. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Minimum contract size
Client registration
SCRA
Prohibition of insider trading
mocks.w: This is Minimum contract size. SEBI prescribes a minimum value for a derivatives contract at the time of its introduction, reviewed periodically, so that lot sizes are meaningful.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: Futures margin limits the loss to the margin amount.
A pair trade buys one related security and sells another, profiting from relative price movement rather than market direction.
The cost of carry is the cost of holding the underlying until expiry, mainly financing cost less any income such as dividends, and drives futures pricing.
A short hedge sells futures to protect against price falls; a long hedge buys futures to protect against price rises.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Because only margin is paid upfront, futures offer leverage: a small price change can produce a large percentage gain or loss on margin.

mocks.p: Which statement about “Exchange-traded derivative” is correct?
o: Exchange-traded derivatives have standardised terms, are cleared by a clearing corporation and carry lower counterparty risk.
Exchange-traded derivatives are customised for each buyer.
A hedger aims to maximise profit from price moves.
Leverage reduces the risk of losses.
mocks.w: Correct: Exchange-traded derivatives have standardised terms, are cleared by a clearing corporation and carry lower counterparty risk.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: A European option holder may exercise any day.
Gamma measures how much delta changes for a ₹1 move in the underlying. It is highest for at-the-money options near expiry.
A long call's profit at expiry = max(spot − strike, 0) − premium; break-even = strike + premium.
Rho measures the change in an option's price for a 1% change in the interest rate.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: Because European options cannot be exercised early, holders who want to exit before expiry sell the option in the market.

mocks.p: Which of these statements is NOT correct?
o: The option buyer is always obliged to exercise.
The buyer of a call pays a premium and has the right to buy the underlying at the strike. Maximum loss is the premium and the potential profit is unlimited.
The premium depends on spot, strike, time to expiry, volatility, interest rates and dividends; higher volatility and longer time raise it.
A European option can be exercised only on the expiry date. All options on Indian exchanges are European style.
mocks.w: That statement is a common misunderstanding. The accurate position: When a buyer exercises, a seller is assigned at random or by rule and must perform the obligation under the contract.

mocks.p: The sensitivity of delta is greatest for options near the strike. Which idea does this illustrate?
o: Gamma
Long put payoff
Option premium determinants
Time value
